title: 125 people sick in third Princess cruise norovirus outbreak this year - AOL.com

analysis.time: The outbreak occurred during the voyage dates of June 12 through July 2, 2026, as reported by the CDC (N4). The news was published on August 13, 2026 (N1).
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak took place on the Ruby Princess cruise ship, which was sailing an Alaska and Canada voyage round-trip from San Francisco (N5). Among the 3,032 guests, 102 reported being ill, along with 23 crew members (N2).
analysis.event: A norovirus outbreak sickened 125 people aboard the Princess Cruises ship Ruby Princess, marking the cruise line’s third such incident in 2026 (N1). The CDC confirmed the outbreak, and Princess Cruises stated that a limited number of guests reported mild gastrointestinal illness (N6).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak affected 102 guests and 23 crew members, totaling 125 individuals. The CDC noted that norovirus accounts for just 1% of all outbreaks reported in 2026 (N13).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Princess Cruises implemented enhanced sanitation protocols and isolated sick passengers and employees, as stated by the CDC (N7, N8). The ship arrived in San Francisco as planned and will undergo comprehensive cleaning before its next cruise (N9). The CDC has logged seven outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships that met its threshold for public notification in 2026 (N10).

analysis.brief_en: A norovirus outbreak aboard the Princess Cruises ship Ruby Princess sickened 125 people, including 102 guests and 23 crew members, during its Alaska and Canada voyage from June 12 to July 2, 2026. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed the outbreak, which marks the cruise line’s third such incident in 2026. Princess Cruises responded by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols and isolating affected individuals. The ship arrived in San Francisco as planned and will undergo comprehensive cleaning before its next cruise. The CDC noted that norovirus accounts for just 1% of all outbreaks reported in 2026, highlighting the relatively low prevalence of the virus compared to other pathogens. The outbreak underscores the challenges of managing gastrointestinal illnesses in confined spaces like cruise ships, where close contact increases the risk of transmission.
